blocks.accepted_litex:
struct Field<K nonempty_set>:
    zero K
    one K
    add fn(x, y K) K
    neg fn(x K) K
    mul fn(x, y K) K
    inv fn(x K) K
    <=>:
        zero != one
        forall x, y, z K:
            add(add(x, y), z) = add(x, add(y, z))
            mul(mul(x, y), z) = mul(x, mul(y, z))
            mul(x, add(y, z)) = add(mul(x, y), mul(x, z))
        forall x, y K:
            add(x, y) = add(y, x)
            mul(x, y) = mul(y, x)
        forall x K:
            add(zero, x) = x
            add(x, neg(x)) = zero
            mul(one, x) = x
        forall x K:
            x != zero
            =>:
                mul(x, inv(x)) = one
blocks.reusable_lesson: A Field structure can use the verified LADR ScalarSystem law surface directly; session source must be byte-framed even when it is wrapped in try.

blocks.intent: Package a vector carrier, its field value, vector operations, and the LADR vector-space laws.
blocks.accepted_litex:
struct VectorSpace<K, V nonempty_set>:
    field &Field<K>
    zero V
    add fn(x, y V) V
    smul fn(a K, x V) V
    <=>:
        forall x, y, z V:
            add(add(x, y), z) = add(x, add(y, z))
        forall x, y V:
            add(x, y) = add(y, x)
        forall x V:
            add(zero, x) = x
            exist y V st {add(x, y) = zero}
        forall a, b K, x V:
            smul(field.mul(a, b), x) = smul(a, smul(b, x))
            smul(field.add(a, b), x) = add(smul(a, x), smul(b, x))
        forall a K, x, y V:
            smul(a, add(x, y)) = add(smul(a, x), smul(a, y))
        forall x V:
            smul(field.one, x) = x
blocks.reusable_lesson: The vector space owns one Field<K> value, so downstream scalar laws remain coherent without repeating six scalar-operation parameters.

blocks.intent: Show that the vector-space zero is the unique additive identity.
dependencies: B002 VectorSpace<K,V> additive identity and commutativity laws
blocks.accepted_litex:
thm additive_identity_unique:
    ? forall K, V nonempty_set, space &VectorSpace<K, V>, identity_candidate V:
        forall x V:
            space.add(identity_candidate, x) = x
        =>:
            identity_candidate = space.zero
    space.add(identity_candidate, space.zero) = space.zero
    space.add(identity_candidate, space.zero) = space.add(space.zero, identity_candidate) = identity_candidate
blocks.reusable_lesson: The LADR two-line identity-uniqueness proof verifies unchanged over the Field-owned vector-space structure.

blocks.intent: Upgrade additive-inverse existence from the structure law to unique existence.
dependencies: B002 VectorSpace<K,V> associativity, commutativity, identity, and inverse existence
blocks.accepted_litex:
thm additive_inverse_exists_unique:
    ? forall K, V nonempty_set, space &VectorSpace<K, V>, x V:
        exist! y V st {space.add(x, y) = space.zero}
    obtain y from exist y V st {space.add(x, y) = space.zero}
    forall y1, y2 V:
        space.add(x, y1) = space.zero
        space.add(x, y2) = space.zero
        =>:
            space.add(y2, x) = space.add(x, y2) = space.zero
            y1 = space.add(space.zero, y1) = space.add(space.add(y2, x), y1) = space.add(y2, space.add(x, y1)) = space.add(y2, space.zero) = space.add(space.zero, y2) = y2
    witness exist! y2 V st {space.add(x, y2) = space.zero} from y
blocks.reusable_lesson: Existence stays a structure law; uniqueness is proved once before exposing canonical vector negation.

blocks.intent: Expose the unique additive inverse as a callable vector_neg function family.

blocks.accepted_litex:
thm add_left_cancel:
    ? forall K, V nonempty_set, space &VectorSpace<K, V>, x, y, z V:
        space.add(x, y) = space.add(x, z)
        =>:
            y = z
    by thm vector_neg_spec(K, V, space, x)
    space.add(\vector_neg<K, V, space>(x), x) = space.add(x, \vector_neg<K, V, space>(x)) = space.zero
    space.add(\vector_neg<K, V, space>(x), space.add(x, y)) = space.add(space.add(\vector_neg<K, V, space>(x), x), y)
    space.add(space.add(\vector_neg<K, V, space>(x), x), y) = space.add(space.zero, y) = y
    space.add(\vector_neg<K, V, space>(x), space.add(x, z)) = space.add(space.add(\vector_neg<K, V, space>(x), x), z)
    space.add(space.add(\vector_neg<K, V, space>(x), x), z) = space.add(space.zero, z) = z
    y = space.add(\vector_neg<K, V, space>(x), space.add(x, y)) = space.add(\vector_neg<K, V, space>(x), space.add(x, z)) = z
blocks.reusable_lesson: After calculating both cancellation endpoints, current verification needs one explicit equality chain that transports the premise through the common left-addition context.

blocks.accepted_litex:
thm zero_scalar_times_vector:
    ? forall K, V nonempty_set, space &VectorSpace<K, V>, x V:
        space.smul(space.field.zero, x) = space.zero
    have p V = space.smul(space.field.zero, x)
    space.field.add(space.field.zero, space.field.zero) = space.field.zero
    space.smul(space.field.add(space.field.zero, space.field.zero), x) = space.smul(space.field.zero, x) = p
    space.smul(space.field.add(space.field.zero, space.field.zero), x) = space.add(space.smul(space.field.zero, x), space.smul(space.field.zero, x)) = space.add(p, p)
    p = space.add(p, p)
    space.add(p, space.zero) = space.add(space.zero, p) = p
    space.add(p, p) = space.add(p, space.zero)
    by thm add_left_cancel(K, V, space, p, p, space.zero) => p = space.zero
blocks.reusable_lesson: For nested structure-field functions, materialize the inner scalar equality inside one continuous smul chain before rewriting the named outer value.

blocks.intent: Prove that every scalar sends vector zero to vector zero.
blocks.accepted_litex:
thm scalar_times_zero_vector:
    ? forall K, V nonempty_set, space &VectorSpace<K, V>, a K:
        space.smul(a, space.zero) = space.zero
    have q V = space.smul(a, space.zero)
    space.add(space.zero, space.zero) = space.zero
    space.smul(a, space.add(space.zero, space.zero)) = space.smul(a, space.zero) = q
    space.smul(a, space.add(space.zero, space.zero)) = space.add(space.smul(a, space.zero), space.smul(a, space.zero)) = space.add(q, q)
    q = space.add(q, q)
    space.add(q, space.zero) = space.add(space.zero, q) = q
    space.add(q, q) = space.add(q, space.zero)
    by thm add_left_cancel(K, V, space, q, q, space.zero) => q = space.zero
blocks.reusable_lesson: The same cancellation spine proves a*0=0 once the outer smul calculation is kept in one explicit equality chain.

blocks.intent: Define a linear map between arbitrary vector spaces over one equal field value.
blocks.accepted_litex:
prop is_linear_map(K, V, W nonempty_set, source &VectorSpace<K, V>, target &VectorSpace<K, W>, T fn(v V) W):
    source.field = target.field
    forall u, v V:
        T(source.add(u, v)) = target.add(T(u), T(v))
    forall a K, v V:
        T(source.smul(a, v)) = target.smul(a, T(v))
blocks.reusable_lesson: The public linear-map concept is a relation on supplied spaces and a callable function; equal field values state the shared scalar semantics.

blocks.intent: Define the closure property of a supplied subset of an arbitrary vector space.
blocks.accepted_litex:
prop is_subspace(K, V nonempty_set, space &VectorSpace<K, V>, U power_set(V)):
    space.zero $in U
    forall u, v V:
        u $in U
        v $in U
        =>:
            space.add(u, v) $in U
    forall a K, v V:
        v $in U
        =>:
            space.smul(a, v) $in U
blocks.reusable_lesson: Subspace remains a property of an existing set; nonemptiness follows from zero membership and need not be a redundant clause.

blocks.intent: Tracer: prove that every abstract linear map sends source zero to target zero.
blocks.accepted_litex:
thm linear_map_sends_zero_to_zero:
    ? forall K, V, W nonempty_set, source &VectorSpace<K, V>, target &VectorSpace<K, W>, T fn(v V) W:
        $is_linear_map(K, V, W, source, target, T)
        =>:
            T(source.zero) = target.zero
    source.add(source.zero, source.zero) = source.zero
    T(source.add(source.zero, source.zero)) = target.add(T(source.zero), T(source.zero))
    target.add(T(source.zero), T(source.zero)) = T(source.add(source.zero, source.zero)) = T(source.zero)
    target.add(T(source.zero), target.zero) = target.add(target.zero, T(source.zero)) = T(source.zero)
    target.add(T(source.zero), T(source.zero)) = target.add(T(source.zero), target.zero)
    by thm add_left_cancel(K, W, target, T(source.zero), T(source.zero), target.zero) => T(source.zero) = target.zero
blocks.reusable_lesson: Zero preservation needs only additive preservation and target cancellation; no coordinate carrier, scalar arithmetic, or field-projection bridge is involved.

blocks.intent: Prove that an abstract linear map preserves the selected additive inverse.
blocks.accepted_litex:
thm linear_map_sends_neg_to_neg:
    ? forall K, V, W nonempty_set, source &VectorSpace<K, V>, target &VectorSpace<K, W>, T fn(v V) W, x V:
        $is_linear_map(K, V, W, source, target, T)
        =>:
            T(\vector_neg<K, V, source>(x)) = \vector_neg<K, W, target>(T(x))
    by thm vector_neg_spec(K, V, source, x)
    by thm vector_neg_spec(K, W, target, T(x))
    by thm linear_map_sends_zero_to_zero(K, V, W, source, target, T)
    T(source.add(x, \vector_neg<K, V, source>(x))) = target.add(T(x), T(\vector_neg<K, V, source>(x)))
    T(source.add(x, \vector_neg<K, V, source>(x))) = T(source.zero) = target.zero
    target.add(T(x), T(\vector_neg<K, V, source>(x))) = target.zero
    target.add(T(x), \vector_neg<K, W, target>(T(x))) = target.zero
    target.add(T(x), T(\vector_neg<K, V, source>(x))) = target.add(T(x), \vector_neg<K, W, target>(T(x)))
    by thm add_left_cancel(K, W, target, T(x), T(\vector_neg<K, V, source>(x)), \vector_neg<K, W, target>(T(x))) => T(\vector_neg<K, V, source>(x)) = \vector_neg<K, W, target>(T(x))
blocks.reusable_lesson: Map the inverse equation to target zero, compare it with the target's canonical inverse equation, and cancel once; no coordinate negation is needed.

thm injective_linear_map_has_trivial_kernel:
    ? forall K, V, W nonempty_set, source &VectorSpace<K, V>, target &VectorSpace<K, W>, T fn(v V) W:
        $is_linear_map(K, V, W, source, target, T)
        $injective(V, W, T)
        =>:
            \linear_kernel<V, W, target.zero, T> = \zero_subspace<V, source.zero>
    by thm linear_map_sends_zero_to_zero(K, V, W, source, target, T)
    by def:
        ? $injective(V, W, T)
    \linear_kernel<V, W, target.zero, T> = {x V: T(x) = target.zero}
    \zero_subspace<V, source.zero> = {source.zero}
    by extension:
        ? \linear_kernel<V, W, target.zero, T> = \zero_subspace<V, source.zero>
        forall x \linear_kernel<V, W, target.zero, T>:
            T(x) = target.zero = T(source.zero)
            x = source.zero
            x $in {source.zero}
            x $in \zero_subspace<V, source.zero>
        forall x \zero_subspace<V, source.zero>:
            x = source.zero
            T(x) = T(source.zero) = target.zero
            x $in \linear_kernel<V, W, target.zero, T>

blocks.intent: Construct the builtin real numbers as the first concrete Field instance.
blocks.accepted_litex:
have fn real_inv(x R) R by cases:
    case x = 0: 0
    case x != 0: 1 / x

have fn real_add(x, y R) R = x + y
have fn real_neg(x R) R = -x
have fn real_mul(x, y R) R = x * y

claim:
    ? forall x R:
        x != 0
        =>:
            real_mul(x, real_inv(x)) = 1
    real_inv(x) = 1 / x
    real_mul(x, real_inv(x)) = x * real_inv(x) = x * (1 / x) = 1

claim:
    ? forall x, y, z R:
        real_add(real_add(x, y), z) = real_add(x, real_add(y, z))
        real_mul(real_mul(x, y), z) = real_mul(x, real_mul(y, z))
        real_mul(x, real_add(y, z)) = real_add(real_mul(x, y), real_mul(x, z))
    real_add(x, y) = x + y
    real_add(y, z) = y + z
    real_add(real_add(x, y), z) = real_add(x, y) + z = (x + y) + z = x + (y + z) = x + real_add(y, z) = real_add(x, real_add(y, z))
    real_mul(x, y) = x * y
    real_mul(x, z) = x * z
    real_mul(y, z) = y * z
    real_mul(real_mul(x, y), z) = real_mul(x, y) * z = (x * y) * z = x * (y * z) = x * real_mul(y, z) = real_mul(x, real_mul(y, z))
    real_mul(x, real_add(y, z)) = x * real_add(y, z) = x * (y + z) = x * y + x * z
    real_add(real_mul(x, y), real_mul(x, z)) = real_mul(x, y) + real_mul(x, z) = x * y + x * z
    real_mul(x, real_add(y, z)) = real_add(real_mul(x, y), real_mul(x, z))

claim:
    ? forall x, y R:
        real_add(x, y) = real_add(y, x)
        real_mul(x, y) = real_mul(y, x)
    real_add(x, y) = x + y = y + x = real_add(y, x)
    real_mul(x, y) = x * y = y * x = real_mul(y, x)

claim:
    ? forall x R:
        real_add(0, x) = x
        real_add(x, real_neg(x)) = 0
        real_mul(1, x) = x
    real_add(0, x) = 0 + x = x
